The facts involve two separate torts at the same job site on 1 Oct 2021, cutting grass and leaf raking for Evergreen Grass Care Ltd in Ottawa. Respondeat superior is engaged for torts committed in the course of employment; employer and employee are jointly and severally liable for the loss flowing from that employee’s tort, co-employees are not liable for each other, and third parties are only liable if they are a legal cause.

Mark – riding mower, pool cover damage
* Mark was operating company equipment to cut grass, an authorised employment task. Distraction by neighbour’s dog, intricate manoeuvres, reaching down from a moving mower with automatic drive, fall and mower running into pool.
* Colleagues 1,10,11,13-17,20-21,2,4-7,9 argue the negligent operation is a negligent mode of performing an authorised task, a momentary careless lapse still closely connected to employment. Evergreen is vicariously liable, Mark personally liable, Evergreen + Mark jointly and severally liable for pool cover / removal / clean-up. Neighbour’s short fence/dog is background, not a legal cause; neighbours are not joint tortfeasors.
* No dissent on Mark’s attribution; all agree Evergreen and Mark jointly and severally liable for Mark’s loss.

Lincoln – blower, scratches to Ferrari
* Lincoln was raking leaves / using blower with company equipment on the lawn area, an authorised task. He admired the Ferrari, disliked Bruce, Bruce absent, rocks in work area blown onto car causing barely noticeable scratches.
* Majority view E: the physical act of blowing the work area with the blower is the ordinary means of performing leaf clearing. Motive/personal animus is irrelevant to vicarious liability; the tort is negligent execution of an authorised task with employer’s equipment on work premises during working hours. Evergreen is vicariously liable, Lincoln personally liable, Evergreen + Lincoln jointly and severally liable for the car damage. Minimal damage affects quantum only, de minimis non curat lex does not extinguish liability.
* Minority view C: colleagues 12,18,19,3,8 argue the facts point to intentional/reckless misuse motivated by personal animus and opportunistic timing with Bruce absent. That is an intentional tort / personal frolic/detour not closely connected to employer’s business, so Evergreen is not vicariously liable; liability rests on Lincoln alone. Minimal damage still compensable but only Lincoln liable.
* The key dispute is whether personal dislike + Bruce’s absence converts negligent leaf blowing into a frolic/intentional wrong outside course of employment. Majority treat motive as irrelevant and the act as negligent performance within scope; minority treat it as personal motive taking it out of scope.

Other points consistently agreed:
* No cross-liability between Mark and Lincoln for each other’s torts.
* Neighbours not jointly and severally liable for Mark’s pool damage; short fence is not a proximate cause.
* Option A wrongly imputes neighbours and says only Lincoln liable for his actions.
* Option B wrongly makes all three defendants jointly and severally for all damage.
* Option D wrongly says minimal damage removes liability.

Current understanding leans to E as the better articulation of Ontario vicarious liability principles: both torts are negligent modes of performing authorised work, closely connected to employment, employer vicariously liable with each employee for his own loss, neighbours not liable. Evergreen Grass Care Ltd is vicarious ly liable under respondeat superior for torts committed by its employees in the course of employment and each employee remains personally liable for the tort he commits. Liability is assessed separately for the two distinct loss events.

Mark
Mark was on Bruce’s property operating a company riding mower in the course of his authorised lawn-care duties. Distraction by the neighbour’s dog, performing intricate movements with the mower and reaching down from a moving mower to pick up a stick, and the fall that led the mower with its automatic drive to continue onto and through the pool cover is negligent operation of equipment in a negligent mode of performing an authorised task. The tort is sufficiently closely connected with the employment to remain in the course of employment; it is not a frolic or detour.

Mark is directly liable for his negligence and Evergreen is vicariously liable for the tort committed by its employee in the course of employment. Evergreen and Mark are jointly and severally liable for the pool cover replacement and clean-up costs.

The neighbours’ unusually short fence and the dog’s return of the stick are background to the distraction. They are not a legal cause of the pool damage and do not make the neighbours joint tortfeasors.

Lincoln
Lincoln was on site raking leaves and using the company blower/rake to work the lawn area next to Bruce’s driveway, i.e. performing his assigned duties with employer’s equipment at work time and place. The factual pleading is that he “went over the area with the blower as he normally would”. Propelling small rocks present in the work area by the blower onto the Ferrari and causing barely noticeable scratches is a negligent manner of performing that authorised work. A foreseeable risk of blowing debris in proximity to adjacent property is inherent to leaf clearing.

Personal motive – Lincoln despising Bruce, admiring the car, Bruce’s absence – does not convert a work-related use of work equipment into a frolic. On Ontario respondeat superior, motive is irrelevant where the physical act is done by means of authorised work and equipment in the course of employment.

Lincoln is personally liable for the negligent use of the blower and Evergreen is vicariously liable for the tort committed in the course of employment. Evergreen and Lincoln are jointly and severally liable for the damage to the Ferrari.

The minimal, barely noticeable nature of the scratches goes to quantum only, not to the existence of liability. Mark is not liable for Lincoln’s loss and Lincoln is not liable for Mark’s loss, and there is no cross liability between them.

3.text:
E

Liability is assessed incident-specifically under Ontario respondeat superior and is employer + committing employee jointly and severally for the loss flowing from that particular tort. Co-employees are not vicariously liable for each other and Bruce’s neighbours are not tortfeasors on these facts.

Mark – riding mower / pool cover
Mark was on Bruce’s property on 1 Oct 2021 operating Evergreen’s riding mower to cut grass, the authorised task he was hired to perform at work time and place with employer equipment. Distraction by the neighbour’s dog, intricate manoeuvres and reaching down from a moving mower with an automatic drive to pick up a stick, the fall with dislocated shoulder and the mower continuing on automatic drive onto and through the pool cover and the consequent removal / clean-up costs are a negligent manner of performing an authorised task. It is a momentary careless lapse so closely connected with the employment that it remains in the course of employment, not a frolic or detour.

Mark is directly liable for his negligence and Evergreen is vicariously liable for a tort committed in the course of employment. Evergreen and Mark are jointly and severally liable for the pool cover replacement, mower removal and clean-up loss. The unusually short fence and the dog’s return of the stick explain the distraction but are not a legal cause of the pool damage and do not make the neighbours joint tortfeasors.

Lincoln – blower / Ferrari
Lincoln was on site at work time on the client’s premises using Evergreen’s blower/rake to clear the assigned leaf area. The facts plead he “went over the area with the blower as he normally would” in a work area immediately adjacent to the driveway that contained small rocks. Propelling those rocks with the blower onto Bruce’s Ferrari and causing barely noticeable scratches is a negligent execution of an authorised leaf/debris clearing task. Propelling loose material against adjacent property is a foreseeable risk of blower use in yard maintenance.

Personal motive – Lincoln despising Bruce, admiring the car, Bruce being absent – goes to state of mind and fault but does not sever the close connection for vicarious liability. The physical act complained of is the use of work equipment to clear the assigned work area in the normal manner of the job, at work time and place in furtherance of Evergreen’s business. There is no abandonment, frolic, detour or pleaded intentional aimed strike; it is negligent performance of an authorised task.

Lincoln is personally liable for the negligent use of the blower and Evergreen is vicariously liable for a tort committed in the course of employment. Evergreen and Lincoln are jointly and severally liable for the Ferrari scratch loss. The minimal/barely noticeable character of the damage goes to quantum only; de minimis does not defeat liability.

Hence:
* Evergreen + Mark jointly and severally liable for the damage resulting from Mark’s actions;
* Evergreen + Lincoln jointly and severally liable for the damage resulting from Lincoln’s actions.

No cross-liability between Mark and Lincoln and no liability of Bruce’s neighbours. That is option E.

6.text:
E

Ontario respondeat superior is incident-specific. An employer is vicariously liable for a tort of an employee that is so closely connected with the employment that it is fairly and properly attributable to the employer, and the committing employee remains directly liable for his own tort. The employer and the committing employee are therefore jointly and severally liable for the loss flowing from that particular tort. Co-employees are not vicariously liable for each other and Bruce’s neighbours are not tortfeasors for the pool loss.

Mark – pool / mower
Mark was on Bruce’s property on 1 Oct 2021 operating Evergreen’s riding mower to cut grass, the authorised lawn-care task, at work time and place with employer equipment. Distraction by the neighbour’s dog, intricate manoeuvres, reaching down from a moving mower with an automatic drive to pick up a stick, the fall and dislocation, and the mower continuing under automatic drive onto and through the pool cover are a negligent manner of performing an authorised task. It is a momentary careless lapse so closely connected with the employment that it remains in the course of employment, not a frolic or detour.

Mark is directly liable for his negligence and Evergreen is vicariously liable. Evergreen and Mark are jointly and severally liable for the pool cover replacement, mower removal and clean-up. The unusually short fence and the dog explain the distraction but are not a legal cause of the pool damage and do not make the neighbours joint tortfeasors.

Lincoln – Ferrari scratches
Lincoln was on site at work time on the client’s premises using Evergreen’s blower/rake to clear the assigned leaf area adjacent to the driveway. The pleaded fact is he “went over the area with the blower as he normally would”. Propelling small rocks present in the work area with the blower onto the adjacent Ferrari and causing barely noticeable scratches is a negligent execution of an authorised leaf/debris clearing task with employer equipment at work time and place. Propelling loose material against adjacent property is a foreseeable risk of blower work.

Personal motive – Lincoln despising Bruce, admiring the Ferrari, Bruce being absent – goes to state of mind and fault but does not sever the close connection. Ontario vicarious liability focuses on the closeness of connection between the employment and the physical act, not the purity of motive. The physical act is the use of work equipment to perform the assigned work in the normal manner of the job. There is no abandonment, frolic, detour or pleaded intentional aimed strike; the damage flows from negligent performance of an authorised task.

Lincoln is personally liable and Evergreen is vicariously liable for a tort committed in the course of employment. Evergreen and Lincoln are jointly and severally liable for the Ferrari scratch loss. The minimal/barely noticeable character of the damage goes to quantum only; de minimis does not extinguish liability.

Liability is therefore bifurcated and incident-specific:
* Evergreen + Mark jointly and severally liable for the damage resulting from Mark’s actions;
* Evergreen + Lincoln jointly and severally liable for the damage resulting from Lincoln’s actions.
No cross-liability between Mark and Lincoln and no liability of Bruce’s neighbours.
